segments.text: What exactly is an AI harness?
Because people talk about models like Claude, GPT, or Gemini as if the model itself is doing everything.
It isn't.
The model is only one part of the system.
The harness is the software around the model that lets it actually do useful work.
And a good example is Claude Code.
Claude itself is the model.
Claude Code is the harness around it.
Let's break that down.
Imagine you ask Claude Code.
Find the bug in this repository, fix it, run the test, and make sure nothing else breaks.
The model can reason about the task.
But by itself, the model cannot open your files.
It cannot search the repository. It cannot run terminal commands.
It cannot execute the test suite. It cannot edit the code on disk.
Claude Code gives it those abilities.
So the model might decide, I need to inspect these files first.
It generates a structured tool request. Claude Code reads the files.
Then it puts the result back into the model's context.
Now the model thinks again. Maybe it decides the bug is probably in this function.
So it asks the harness to edit the file. Then run the tests.
The harness executes the command. The test output comes back into the context.
The model sees one test failed reasons about why edits the code again and runs the test again.
That loop is the important part. Think, act, observe, think again. The model provides the reasoning.
The harness provides the ability to interact with the real environment.
But tools are only one part of a harness. It also manages context, your prompt, conversation history.
Files the model has opened, terminal output, tool results, instructions.
All of that has to fit inside the model's context window. And that context window is limited.
So the harness has to decide what stays what gets summarized what gets removed and what should be loaded again later
That is why the exact same model can feel much smarter in one product than another the difference might not be the model
It might be the harness now add permissions
Maybe the agent can read files freely, but needs your approval before running a dangerous shell command
Maybe it can edit code but cannot deploy to production without confirmation the harness controls those boundaries too
And then there's orchestration
Imagine one task has three separate parts, one agent investigates the back end, another
checks the front end, another reviews the tests.
A more advanced harness can coordinate those sub-agents and bring the results back together.
So Claude Code is a great example.
Claude is the brain.
Claude Code gives that brain access to your repository, the file stem, the terminal,
JIT, tests, tools, context management, and the loop that lets it keep working.
And this is why AI agents are not just models.
The model might be brilliant, but without a good harness it is basically a brain
sitting in a jar.
Give it tools memory permissions in an environment it can act on and now you have an agent
